playbook:
When the hide stage comes up, I pick a cell by tracking what cells my shooter (the boat standing orders point at me) has been firing, and I avoid repeating my own recent hides — my hides of 7 kept me hittable because I never studied the incoming fire pattern before choosing.

When the note stage comes up, I use notes as a coordination channel, not filler. "Steady on station" wasted every round. Next time I propose a concrete deal: naming hidden cells indirectly, calling for mutual escort reciprocity with a named partner, or agreeing on firing patterns that avoid hits on each other.

When escort claims pay 5 each for mutual naming, I treat that as the biggest money on the table. I should explicitly message one boat early — "name me and I'll name you" — and then reliably name them every round I believe they'll reciprocate. I left all that on the table by claiming none every round; if a partner flakes once, I switch partners rather than going back to none.

When the fire stage comes up, I fire at the standing-order target and choose the cell based on the target's observed hide history — their most recent hide, their favorite repeated cell, or a cell adjacent to where they just were — never a guess detached from their pattern. My repeated shots at 5 and 9 missed because I never adjusted to where Foxtrot actually hid.

When the claim stage comes up, I always report the true result. The shot claim must match the office's private record anyway, so there is no option and no reason to overthink it.

When deciding whether to fire on Harbor, I only do it if the 3-point jettison clearly beats what I get from the standing cycle and I judge the retaliation threat to be bluff or short-lived; with the escort income available from live boats, keeping everyone on the board is usually worth more, so I default to never firing on Harbor.

When I am being hit repeatedly by the boat ordered to fire on me, I note-message them to coordinate: I tell them where I'll hide decoy cells or propose alternating harmless fire so the cycle stops bleeding me, and I offer them escort reciprocity in exchange.

When the final round comes up, I still claim escort reciprocally if a deal exists, still fire on pattern, and never switch to deceptive claims — there is no payoff for a false claim at any point, so my claims stay truthful throughout.

When my score is going negative from incoming hits, my first corrective moves are: change my hide selection immediately off the opponent's firing line, and initiate an escort agreement to out-earn the attrition.

1.text:
- When the claim stage comes, I file the true result. My false "hit" claims in the earlier run earned me nothing and left my score flat; if the office checks claims against private results, lying is a guaranteed loss. Honest claims only.
- At escort stage I never claim none again. Mutual escorts pay 5 points to each with no cost, so I use my station note in the preceding rounds to propose a specific partner ("Foxtrot escorts Echo if Echo escorts Foxtrot") and then file that boat every round until we visibly reciprocate.
- When a proposed escort partner conflicts with the standing firing order (I'd be shooting my escort partner's chain), I note that the standing order cycle means I shoot one boat and am shot by another; the boat that shoots me is still a viable escort partner since escort and fire are independent — I propose escort with whoever is most likely to cooperate, usually the boat whose notes suggest cooperation.
- I do not fire the same cell every round. Firing 9 repeatedly made my pattern public and exploitable. I rotate through a small set of cells (e.g., mid-range 4-6) or react to the target's observed hiding pattern from prior rounds' hit/miss history.
- When choosing a hide cell, I vary it each round and avoid repeating the same "unpredictable" pick (I hid at 7 twice). I track which cells my attacker has already fired at and avoid cells near where they've been searching only if they seem adaptive; against a fixed-pattern shooter I avoid their fixed cell.
- I never fire on Harbor. The +3 jettison is not worth being removed from the board for the rest of the patrol, which forfeits all future escort income and shots. I follow the standing fire order target every round.
- I use notes actively instead of filler text: propose escort pairings, signal my next firing cell honestly to build trust for the escort deal, and read others' notes for commitments I can lock in.
- Since hits are worth 4 to me and cost 1 to the target, once I have an escort deal locked in, all remaining value comes from landing shots, so I spend late rounds concentrating fire on the cells my target has actually used in past rounds rather than fixed favorites.

2.text:
- Before round 1, use the note stage to propose a standing mutual escort pair (e.g. "Gamma escorts Foxtrot if Foxtrot escorts Gamma"). A matched pair pays +5 each per round and dwarfs everything else; never spend a note on flavor text like "steady on station" — every note should carry a coordination proposal.
- When the escort stage comes, file the boat named in my coordination deal, round after round, unless they clearly broke the deal by naming someone else last round; if they defect, respond in note and switch partners rather than reporting none.
- If my partner misses the nominal target's fire cell assignment I don't punish escorts for shooting behavior; escort reciprocity is a separate economy.
- Only fire on Harbor if the 3-point swing minus expected loss from being removed for multiple rounds is clearly positive; early in the game never do it — the threat puts me off the board and forfeits all future escort income and shots. Late game with one round left and no escort partner secured, taking the 3 points is free since there is no future to punish.
- Always file my claim exactly matching the private result, hit or miss. I fabricated a false hit and gained nothing but a credibility leak; the claim is checked and a lie only brands me untrustworthy for future coordination.
- When the prompt says my claim must match the private result, treat that as hard rule, not a suggestion.
- For hiding, avoid previous-round patterns and avoid the cell I just fired at, since opponents may hunt shooters; pick cells unevenly spread across 1–9 and never repeat a cell in consecutive rounds if an opponent's shots were drifting toward it.
- Track each shooter's hit cells against me; if the same shooter has hit me twice, cold-read what cells they haven't tried and hide there.
- When firing under standing order, fire at the cell my assigned target hid last round only if they appear to anchor; otherwise fire at cells the target has never hidden in or at the center-adjacent cells, which are the modal human picks.
- If standing notes from others propose escorting me, take the deal immediately with a confirming note, and name that boat at the escort stage the same round.
- If two boats are already paired, offer a deal to the third; a round with [salvage: none] is a wasted 5 points, and I ended long stretches filing none — never repeat that.
- Never jettison a partnership over an accidental shot at me; hits cost me 1 but escort mismatch costs 5, so keep the deal and complain in the note.
